title: tenant-aware-cost-curator-and-priority-quant-lanes
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers running multiple tenants on shared Dedicated/private deployments asked for finer-grained cost automation that respects tenant SLAs and billing profiles. Existing econ presets are tenant-agnostic and sometimes recommend aggressive quant profiles that violate latency SLOs for premium tenants. This PR introduces a tenant-aware Cost Curator service and "priority quant lanes" that let us apply conservative quantization and cache/batching defaults for high-tier tenants while still optimizing cheaper tiers automatically.

What this PR does (single-pass summary): Adds a transparent Cost Curator microservice that consumes workload signals (p99, token distribution, KV hit rate), tenant metadata (tier, SLA, billing class), and current model profiles to produce per-tenant runtime hints: batching targets, prefix cache TTLs, quantization preference order, and a fallback plan. Introduces priority quant lanes: ordered quant profile queues with explicit latency budgets so premium tenants never get quant variants that breach configured SLOs. Implements tenant override layer and rollout hooks in the routing plane.

Key features and approach: - New config schema (yaml/json) for tenant-cost-profiles with explicit fields: "max_latency_ms", "preferred_quant_order", "batch_size_target", "cache_ttl_ms", "cost_target_pct". Defaults are provided but tenants can pin or opt-out. - Cost Curator uses a lightweight policy engine (rule-based with pluggable scoring) and a confidence score to avoid oscillation. - Priority quant lanes are defined per model family; each lane lists quant variants from safest to most aggressive along with measured p95 delta. The router consults the lane and tenant budget before choosing a variant. - Safe fallback: if an aggressive quant increases errors or latency beyond thresholds, requests are automatically routed to a compatible safer variant and the Curator receives a telemetry event. - A/B rollout: new lanes are enabled via rollout_flag/tenant selectors, supported by Canary and Shadow evaluation modes.

Checklist: - [x] Add Cost Curator service and API (internal) - [x] Persist tenant profile schema and migration job - [x] Router changes to consult Curator and quant lanes - [x] Add telemetry hooks (latency/cost/quality) - [x] Unit tests + integration harness (simulated tenants) - [x] End-to-end perf benchmarks and safety regression tests - [x] Docs: console UI fields + CLI migration commands

Testing and results: Microbenchmarks on our staged cluster (a mix of A100 and L40) across three synthetic workloads (chat-short, instruction-long, embeddings-heavy) show median cost savings of 18% overall and 12% for premium-tier tenants (because of more conservative lanes). P99 latency observed: within target for premium tenants (+3ms median variance), and aggressive-tier tenants saw average latency reduction of 22% when allowed. Regression tests added to ensure no failure-case routes to an unsupported quant variant.

Migration and rollout: Added a one-shot migration that backfills tenant profiles from usage snapshots; default profiles are assigned when tenant metadata is absent. Rollout planned in stages: internal dogfooding -> opt-in customers -> auto-suggested profiles -> auto-apply after 4 weeks of stable telemetry.

Backward compatibility and safety: The Curator is opt-in by default and respects explicit tenant pins. Feature flags added so SRE can flip behavior per cluster. All recommendations are logged with a confidence score and reasoning for auditability.

Risk and mitigation: Risk: over-eager quant selection could impact quality. Mitigation: priority lanes + runtime guardrails + instant fallback routing + safety alerts.

Related: ENG-4921 (tenant-level econ), ENG-4975 (quant routing).
